First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{3}-10{y}^{2}+25y & =0 \\ y({y}^{2}-10y+25) & =0 \\ y(y-5)^{2} & =0 \\ y & =0,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we draw a sketch of the region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082348/assets/593d1168ce7328aa93edd61fcabc116451fcda8ef24faeac0949fa0a8e686b51.png)

We want to find the area between the curve $x={y}^{3}-10{y}^{2}+25y$ and the $y$-axis from  $y=0$ to $y=5.$ To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}\,({y}^{3}-10{y}^{2}+25y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-10{\int }_{0}^{5}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y+25{\int }_{0}^{5}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}|}_{0}^{5}-{\frac{10}{3}{y}^{3}|}_{0}^{5}+{\frac{25}{2}{y}^{2}|}_{0}^{5} \\  & =(\frac{{5}^{4}}{4}-0)-\frac{10}{3}({5}^{3}-0)+\frac{25}{2}({5}^{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{625}{4}-\frac{1250}{3}+\frac{625}{2} \\  & =\frac{625}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
